affected_modalities: Autologous CiPSC islets|Allogeneic donor and stem-cell-derived islets|Hypoimmune cells
observed_evidence: One edited donor-islet recipient had graft function without immunosuppression through 14 months [S5/S8; same recipient]. Humanized autoimmune mice showed avoidance of autoimmune killing [S16; abstract only]. The autologous CiPSC case was already immunosuppressed for a liver transplant, preventing assessment of graft immune responses [S11].
population_or_model: Human: one UP421 recipient and one distinct autologous CiPSC recipient. Animal: autologous diabetic humanized autoimmune mice; counts and duration unavailable in the reviewed abstract.
human_relevance: Relevant to human replacement-cell survival, but animal protection and human graft persistence do not establish control of human autoimmune memory.
hypothesized_mechanism: Autoreactive memory might persist despite cell replacement or reduced allo-recognition; recurrence and protection by editing are not established in the cited human cases.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary source and claim-fit design (2/5). Clinical recurrence endpoint, adequate human sample/follow-up, and independent replication are absent; this scores the bounded observation, not proof of the hypothesis.
unresolved_questions: Which autoreactive pathways persist, and do they precede human graft-function loss? Missing: longitudinal autoreactive-cell measurements paired with graft function across recipients.
competing_explanations: If graft loss occurs, alloimmunity, ischemia, inadequate cell mass, or product effects could resemble autoimmunity; ongoing immunosuppression confounds the CiPSC case.
next_discriminating_test: Test within-model edited versus unedited grafts with autoreactive immune and graft-function measurements; require independent biological units and replication before human inference.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: graft protection is central and loss could harm recipients; gap 3: human recurrence unresolved; data/computation/tractability 2: named preclinical sources but unverified reusable data and indirect translation.
candidate_data: S16 supplementary data are a candidate only; access, reuse terms, independent animals, controls, and longitudinal metadata unverified.

observed_evidence: Lantidra labeling reports serious adverse reactions in 27/30 recipients over variable follow-up of 0.3-14.5 years and loss of islet-cell function after immunosuppression discontinuation in 8/30; the latter is not 8 out of all discontinuers [S13]. Zimislecel and PEC-Direct also used systemic immunosuppression and reported serious events [S3/S19].
population_or_model: Selected adults in two pooled Lantidra single-arm studies (30), zimislecel phase 1-2 follow-up (14), and an optimized PEC-Direct group (10).
human_relevance: Observed human harms and treatment dependence are directly relevant, but regimens, procedures, exposure, and follow-up differ and do not provide comparative causal risks.
hypothesized_mechanism: Drug exposure may contribute to infection, malignancy, toxicity, and discontinuation; attribution and magnitude must be separated from procedural and background risks.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary/authoritative source, claim-fit design, and patient-important endpoint (3/5). Adequate comparative sample/follow-up and independent confirmation of causal attribution are not established.
unresolved_questions: Which events are drug-, procedure-, or background-related? Missing: harmonized participant-level event timing, exposure, discontinuation denominators, and comparator data.
competing_explanations: Selection, concomitant illness, regimen differences, surgery, and differential follow-up can explain apparent safety differences.
next_discriminating_test: Pair adverse-event, exposure, and graft-function timelines; report event attribution as supplied and assess censoring/missingness before any comparative analysis.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: direct harms and treatment dependence; gap 2: human harms observed but attribution unresolved; data 3: cataloged aggregate outcomes; computation 1: current aggregates cannot identify causal drug effects; tractability 2: participant data needed.
candidate_data: S13 and published reports provide aggregate outcomes. S20 has posted registry results; S4 had none at the cataloged check. Individual-level data and reuse permissions are unverified.

affected_modalities: Closed macroencapsulation|Open vascularized devices|Prevascularized donor-islet scaffolds
observed_evidence: VC-01 was terminated for insufficient functional engraftment; 19 entered Cohort 1 and no one entered the planned efficacy Cohort 2 [S17]. Open-device reports show C-peptide production, not direct proof of an oxygenation mechanism [S18/S19]. Encellin lists fibrosis/containment endpoints without posted results at the cataloged check [S22].
population_or_model: Human: VC-01 Cohort 1 (19); PEC-Direct report (17) and optimized group (10) within NCT03163511, not independent trials. Encellin and Cell Pouch are registered human protocols, not observed efficacy datasets.
human_relevance: Clinical graft-function limitations are relevant, but no causal oxygenation/fibrosis conclusion follows. Candidate in-vitro human-islet data are a stress-response proxy, not a graft/device test.
hypothesized_mechanism: Oxygen/nutrient transport, vascularization, or fibrosis might constrain function; the reviewed human program outcomes do not establish these as the cause.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary/official sources and claim-fit design (2/5). C-peptide is not itself patient benefit; direct mechanism measures, adequate causal sample, and independent mechanism replication are missing.
unresolved_questions: Which paired perfusion, oxygenation, fibrosis, viable-cell-mass, and function measurements discriminate mechanisms? Missing: direct product-level mechanism data and matched comparators.
competing_explanations: Cell potency/dose, immune injury, implantation site, surgery, and measurement differences can produce similar low-function signals.
next_discriminating_test: Pair device-level oxygenation/perfusion and explant histology with graft-function endpoints by product. Separately test donor-aware in-vitro stress signatures as a proxy, without attributing device failures.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: graft-function loss; gap 3: causal mechanisms unresolved; data 2: stress dataset identifiable but reuse unverified; computation/tractability 2: measurable proxy exists but direct device inference needs new data.
candidate_data: GEO GSE218316 [S25] official metadata identify three non-diabetic human donors, stress treatments including hypoxia, untreated controls, and listed count/metadata files. Files, reuse terms, donor-condition balance, and independent validation still need Issue #14 verification.

failure_mode: Loss of graft function and limited durability
observed_evidence: Lantidra labeling reports loss of function after immunosuppression cessation in 8/30 and insulin independence beyond five years in 9/30 over variable follow-up of 0.3-14.5 years [S13]. Zimislecel reports insulin independence in 10/12 full-dose recipients at day 365 [S3]; UP421 reports function, not insulin independence, in the same single recipient through 14 months [S5/S8].
population_or_model: Human: Lantidra pooled treated cohort (30); zimislecel safety sample (14) and full-dose outcome denominator (12); one UP421 recipient with repeated reports.
human_relevance: Clinical outcomes are relevant to durability but cannot be pooled across follow-up, products, definitions, repeat infusions, or immunosuppression. Short observation is a gap, not demonstrated graft failure.
hypothesized_mechanism: Attrition, immune injury, metabolic stress, inadequate mass, or co-intervention withdrawal could reduce function; a common cross-product durability mechanism is unproven.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary/authoritative source, claim-fit design, and patient-important endpoint (3/5). Comparable long-term sample/follow-up and independent causal replication are lacking.
unresolved_questions: What is the multi-year trajectory of benefit and loss of function? Missing: common longitudinal endpoints, numbers at risk, censoring, retreatment, and exposure histories.
competing_explanations: Initial cell mass, product/dose, endpoint definitions, follow-up length, informative withdrawal, and treatment changes can explain apparent differences.
next_discriminating_test: Analyze product-specific longitudinal insulin use, C-peptide, HbA1c/CGM, and severe hypoglycemia with censoring/exposure histories; use a common horizon only when denominators support it.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: loss of clinical benefit; gap 2: human trajectories partly reported; data 3: accessible aggregate outcomes; computation/tractability 2: reliable trajectory analysis needs unconfirmed participant-level follow-up.
candidate_data: S3/S13 are candidate aggregate-extraction sources; S5/S8 are one cohort, not replication. Harmonized participant-level follow-up data are not confirmed.

failure_mode: Tumorigenicity, off-target differentiation, and immune-surveillance escape
observed_evidence: Undifferentiated hypoimmune iPSCs formed teratomatous multi-lineage growths in rhesus experiments [S14; not a purified clinical islet product]. A humanized-mouse abstract reports anti-CD47 elimination of HIP pseudoislet cells [S16]; no validated human removal strategy follows.
population_or_model: Animal: undifferentiated rhesus HIP iPSCs implanted in four allogeneic rhesus macaques (distinct from islet-transplant experiments); human HIP pseudoislets in humanized mice with abstract-only counts/duration unavailable.
human_relevance: The undifferentiated-cell observation motivates product-specific safety testing, not an estimated tumor incidence for differentiated human islet products. Human selectivity and completeness of removal remain unknown.
hypothesized_mechanism: Residual undifferentiated cells, genomic changes, or reduced immune surveillance might create risks; clinical-grade product risk and human removal-control safety remain unknown.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary sources and claim-fit preclinical designs (2/5). Human patient-important safety endpoint, adequate clinical follow-up, and independent clinical confirmation are absent.
unresolved_questions: Which purity/genomic measures predict risk? Missing: differentiated-product tumor incidence, long-term surveillance, and human removal completeness/selectivity.
competing_explanations: Undifferentiated versus purified cells, dose, site, and model biology may account for growth; mouse cell elimination does not establish safety for other CD47-expressing host cells.
next_discriminating_test: Test differentiated-product release assays and long-term model outcomes; quantify removal completeness, selectivity, and host off-target effects with matched positive/negative controls.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: potentially serious harm; gap 3: clinical product risk unresolved; data/computation/tractability 2: named studies and bounded assays but unverified usable data and translation.
candidate_data: S14/S16 supplementary and assay-level data are candidates only; availability/reuse and applicability to clinical-grade differentiated products are unverified.

failure_mode: Manufacturing scale, potency, and lot consistency
affected_modalities: Donor-derived islets|Stem-cell-derived islets|Gene-edited cells|Encapsulated cell products
observed_evidence: FDA's nonbinding draft CGT guidance describes manufacturing process design/control, material control, in-process testing, and lot-release assays as a potency-assurance strategy [S24]. Lantidra is made from deceased-donor islets [S1/S13]. No comparative lot-failure rate or manufacturing-capacity dataset was identified in the reviewed sources.
population_or_model: General human cellular/gene-therapy development guidance, not an islet-specific clinical dataset. Lantidra labeling concerns human deceased-donor islet product.
human_relevance: Potency assurance is relevant to human product development, but general guidance is not proof of manufacturing failure in any islet product. Donor sourcing and stem-cell scale-up are different problems.
hypothesized_mechanism: Differentiation, editing, purification, storage, loading, or assay variation could affect consistency; no particular manufacturing cause is demonstrated by the reviewed clinical outcomes.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: authoritative source and fit for the narrow regulatory/material-origin claim (2/5). Patient-important endpoint, adequate clinical mechanism dataset, and independent outcome replication are not supplied by guidance.
unresolved_questions: Can lot-release potency predict clinical function? Missing: product-linked yields, failed lots, release criteria, capacity, costs, and outcome linkage.
competing_explanations: Platform-specific processes and starting materials differ; donor-derived sourcing constraints cannot be assumed for renewable cell inputs.
next_discriminating_test: Compare lot-level potency/identity/viability/purity with outcomes within one product if lawful data are released; first verify availability and assay comparability.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: product performance and release quality; gap 3: critical lot-level data missing; data/tractability 1: no named reusable lot-outcome dataset; computation 2: bounded analysis possible only if such data emerge.
candidate_data: No product-linked public lot-level potency/outcome dataset identified in the cited scoping sources; do not infer that none exists elsewhere.

observed_evidence: Zimislecel's reported analyses were interim and not prespecified [S3]. Current registry endpoints and published endpoints are not interchangeable [S3/S4]. FDA's Stage 3 teplizumab indication uses C-peptide as a surrogate under accelerated approval [S6/S26]. The Issue #3 audit separately records the Stage 2 TN-10 clinical-onset endpoint, Stage 3 PROTECT C-peptide endpoint, and postapproval study [S27-S31]; preservation is not reversal of established T1D.
population_or_model: Human: zimislecel phase 1-2 (14; full-dose outcome sample 12); teplizumab Stage 2 onset-delay and Stage 3 preservation trials in separate populations; product-specific registry protocols/results.
human_relevance: Endpoint interpretation affects human benefit claims. Preserve disease stage, intervention, outcome definition, assessment window, and analysis population; a biomarker or protocol is not observed clinical benefit.
hypothesized_mechanism: Surrogate inflation, endpoint drift, or incompatible definitions can create misleading apparent differences; these are interpretive risks, not biological failure mechanisms.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary/authoritative source and fit for endpoint/reporting claims (2/5). This is a methods row, not a patient-benefit estimate; patient-important benefit, adequate causal sample, and independent benefit replication are not established.
unresolved_questions: Which outcomes can be harmonized? Remaining gaps include consistent timing, denominator, missingness/censoring, and endpoint hierarchy across treatment and disease-stage comparisons.
competing_explanations: Population, product, phase, follow-up, and interim analyses may explain apparent differences; unavailable results are not null results.
next_discriminating_test: Map endpoints/time windows/denominators to the minimum-outcomes rubric; report how conclusions change when incomparable outcomes or overlapping cohorts are excluded.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 2: indirect risk of misleading inference; gap 2: definitions partly available; data/computation/tractability 3: structured local records and bounded reproducible endpoint audit exist.
candidate_data: Local evidence.csv plus official registry records [S4/S9/S17/S20/S28/S30/S31] support aggregate methods research, not cross-trial causal efficacy comparison; participant data remain unconfirmed.

failure_mode: Limited generalizability of early clinical evidence
observed_evidence: Evidence includes small uncontrolled cohorts and one-person reports [S3/S5/S8/S19]. Lantidra's indication is selected adults unable to approach target HbA1c because of recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management and education [S13].
population_or_model: Human: selected Lantidra adults (30), zimislecel follow-up (14), one UP421 recipient, and optimized PEC-Direct adults (10); UP421 publications are repeated observation of one person.
human_relevance: These populations do not establish benefit/risk in all ages, disease stages, comorbidity groups, or care settings. Lack of subgroup evidence is not evidence of subgroup inefficacy.
hypothesized_mechanism: Disease duration, residual function, comorbidity, age, immune status, or setting might modify outcomes; such effects are not established by these cohorts.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary/authoritative sources and design fit for reported cohort/eligibility facts (2/5). General-population patient benefit, adequate subgroup samples, and independent subgroup confirmation are missing.
unresolved_questions: Who is absent or unreported? Missing: sufficient demographic/subgroup counts, common covariates, participant outcomes, and external cohorts.
competing_explanations: Chance, eligibility/selection, treatment, dose, follow-up, and missingness may resemble effect modification.
next_discriminating_test: First map coverage descriptively; only test prespecified effect modifiers if independent sample size and covariate balance suffice, with external validation.
priority_rationale: Impact 3: broad applicability; safety/gap 2: selected cohorts and incomplete coverage; data/computation/tractability 2: descriptive mapping possible but valid subgroup inference requires more data.
candidate_data: Published cohort/eligibility information is a descriptive candidate; reusable participant-level demographics and outcomes are unconfirmed.

failure_mode: Access, treatment burden, and equitable availability
affected_modalities: Transplant-based cell replacement|Other modalities only with their own access evidence
observed_evidence: Lantidra's narrow indication, portal-vein infusion, potential repeat infusions, and immunosuppression are documented [S1/S13]. The reviewed sources do not establish comparative prices, coverage, geographic availability, or patient-reported burden across modalities.
population_or_model: Human: selected adults eligible for Lantidra; label/approval context rather than a comparative access cohort.
human_relevance: Human access and practical burden matter separately from graft efficacy. Existing product-specific delivery requirements do not quantify affordability or equity.
hypothesized_mechanism: Price, center capacity, eligibility, product supply, travel, and monitoring could limit access; the relative contribution is unknown.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: authoritative sources and fit for indication/procedure claims (2/5). Patient-reported access outcomes, adequate comparative access sample, and independent access confirmation are absent.
unresolved_questions: Who can access which product at what direct/indirect cost? Missing: jurisdiction-specific coverage, supply, travel/caregiver burden, and patient-reported data.
competing_explanations: Jurisdiction, payer, time, eligibility, and supply may explain availability differences; missing data do not imply equitable access or no demand.
next_discriminating_test: Inventory official coverage, centers, supply, and patient-reported burden by jurisdiction and product before any access/cost-effectiveness modeling.
priority_rationale: Impact 3: who can benefit; gap 3: comparative access evidence unresolved; safety 2: burden affects benefit-risk context; data/computation/tractability 1: no bounded comparable dataset established.
candidate_data: No harmonized public comparative access/cost dataset identified in the reviewed sources; Issue #14 must verify candidates before selecting such an analysis.

failure_mode: Product-specific negative programs with unresolved mechanisms
affected_modalities: VX-264 encapsulated stem-cell-derived islets|VC-01 closed macroencapsulation
observed_evidence: VC-01's official reason is insufficient functional product engraftment; Cohort 1 enrolled 19 and efficacy Cohort 2 enrolled none [S17]. Vertex reported VX-264 did not meet its efficacy endpoint and would not advance [S10; sponsor report]; its registry lists 7 actual enrollees but no results at the cataloged check [S9].
population_or_model: Human programs: VC-01 Cohort 1 (19; 9 completed/10 did not), no Cohort 2; VX-264 actual enrollment 7, sponsor efficacy-analysis denominator and outcome counts unavailable.
human_relevance: These are product/program findings, not proof of a common device mechanism or modality-wide ineffectiveness. Enrollment is not an efficacy denominator.
hypothesized_mechanism: Oxygen transport, fibrosis, cell potency/dose, immune exposure, surgery, or other product factors might explain outcomes; available sources cannot rank these mechanisms.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: official/primary reporting and fit for bounded program-status statements (2/5). Detailed patient-important efficacy endpoint data, adequate causal analysis, and replicated mechanism are absent.
unresolved_questions: Which outcome-level/explant/manufacturing measurements exist? Missing: VX-264 analyzed counts, direct mechanisms, and matched comparisons; VC-01 efficacy cohort never enrolled.
competing_explanations: Different products, endpoint definitions, cell inputs, placement, and follow-up could produce similar program decisions without a common biological cause.
next_discriminating_test: Locate primary endpoint-level results and explant data separately for each product; proceed to a mechanism test only if direct measurements distinguish alternatives.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 2: indirect inference risk, not an additional independent biological failure; gap 3: causes unresolved; data 2: named records but detailed data missing; computation 1: mechanism not identifiable; tractability 3: bounded source/data-retrieval task.
candidate_data: S9/S10/S17 identify outcomes; no reusable participant/explant/mechanism dataset is verified. Do not double-count this provenance row as independent evidence for FM-03.

affected_modalities: Allogeneic donor islets|Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets|Hypoimmune gene-edited cells
observed_evidence: Conventional replacement used systemic immunosuppression [S3/S13]. One gene-edited donor-islet recipient had function without immunosuppression through 14 months [S5/S8]. Edited primary rhesus islets survived 40 weeks in one allogeneic macaque, whereas unedited islets were rejected [S14].
population_or_model: Human: zimislecel 14, Lantidra 30, and one UP421 recipient. Animal: edited primary rhesus islets in one allogeneic macaque with a separate unedited recipient; S14 also includes distinct mouse/iPSC experiments.
human_relevance: Allogeneic immune protection is clinically relevant, but one edited human case and model-specific controls cannot estimate broad rejection prevention or prove avoidance of autoimmune recurrence.
hypothesized_mechanism: HLA and other innate/adaptive recognition may injure allogeneic grafts; edits affecting selected pathways may leave other immune mechanisms intact.
confidence_rationale: Framework checks passed: primary/authoritative sources and fit for model-specific observations (2/5). Human patient-important rejection-prevention endpoint, adequate edited-human sample/follow-up, and independent clinical replication are missing.
unresolved_questions: Which alloimmune pathways persist, and how sensitive is monitoring? Missing: multi-recipient human rejection data and product-specific longitudinal immune/function measurements.
competing_explanations: Hypoxia, dose/potency, surgery, and recurrent autoimmunity may resemble rejection; no detected response in one recipient is not proof of no risk.
next_discriminating_test: Test edited versus matched unedited allogeneic grafts within each model using immune monitoring plus function; require independent biological units and human confirmation before generalization.
priority_rationale: Impact/safety 3: graft loss and immune harm; gap 3: broad clinical protection unknown; data/computation/tractability 2: named primary models but unverified sample-level reuse and sparse replication.
candidate_data: S14 supplementary data are a candidate; reusable biological-unit-level controls and files unverified. S5/S8 are one repeated human case and cannot supply independent validation.
